clue.text: Composer with bad flu is perfectly happy

parts.note: Sir Arthur Bliss, the English composer

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters next to it are spoiled into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician who has caught a nasty bout of flu is somehow entirely content.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Bliss was Master of the Queen's Music; his surname is followed by the reshuffled illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Blissful describes a state of complete joy, which is a synonym for being utterly content.

clue.text: Without stress, add one hundred to one hundred

parts.note: a ton is slang for one hundred
Roman numeral one
Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An arithmetic instruction that pretends to be relaxing: a calm sum of hundreds.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is read two ways: once as the slang 'a ton', once as the Roman numerals I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an atonic syllable is one that carries no accent, so it is unstressed.

clue.text: Do one's best to be objective with yobbo

parts.note: an objective is an aim or target
a yobbo is British slang for a rowdy hooligan

explanation.surface: Advice to try hard while staying fair-minded alongside a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like an adjective meaning impartial, but it is the noun meaning target.
explanation.definitionFit: To go all out is an idiom for making every possible effort, giving maximum exertion.

clue.text: Director's call for fighting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a film director shouts to start a take
second meaning: combat, as soldiers seeing it

explanation.surface: A film director shouting to begin a battle scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Film-makers shout this word to start shooting, and military combat is described as soldiers being in it.

clue.text: A Labour leader takes many shares out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so only the opening letter of that party name is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the party name
lots means a great many

explanation.surface: A Labour Party chief grabs a large number of stock holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shares' looks like a noun about stocks, but with 'out' it is the verb phrase defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion portions among several recipients.

clue.text: A broken rib and a gashed head? This should prevent that

definitions.text: A broken rib and a gashed head? This should prevent that

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so those letters are put back together differently

parts.note: the article and the bone, to be rearranged
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the wound word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the injury word

explanation.surface: Car-crash injuries, and the safety device meant to stop them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a cracked rib and a cut head are exactly what this device guards against.
explanation.definitionFit: An air bag inflates in a collision to cushion the occupant and so prevent chest and head injuries.

clue.text: Pained expression when taken in by French article that's disreputable

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: le is a French word for 'the'
the cry someone gives when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone winces on being swallowed up by a shady French item.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche is borrowed from French and describes someone of dubious, rakish morality.

clue.text: The majority of Stevenson's letters are all the same

indicators.note: most of the name's letters are wanted, so the run sits inside it with just a few dropped from the ends

parts.note: the six letters left after dropping the outer ones of the surname

explanation.surface: A remark that most of Robert Louis Stevenson's correspondence is monotonous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence but means the letters of the name itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so is a concessive phrase meaning nevertheless, which is what 'all the same' also expresses.

clue.text: Recipe mania may be the source of a popular song

indicators.note: mania is frenzied madness, so the word beside it goes wild and its letters scramble

parts.note: every letter of both words is rearranged

explanation.surface: A craze for cookery instructions might inspire a hit tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mania' is both indicator and part of the fodder, a liberty some setters take; the whole of 'Recipe mania' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: American Pie is Don McLean's 1971 hit, an eight-minute ballad that topped the charts.

clue.text: Porn is circulating in jail

indicators.note: things circulating move round and round, so the letters get moved into a new order

parts.note: both words rearranged together

explanation.surface: Pornographic material is being passed around behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Jail and prison are synonyms for an institution where convicted offenders are locked up.

clue.text: Men circumnavigating 504 islands

indicators.note: to circumnavigate is to sail all the way round, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: men are males
Roman numerals D (500) and IV (4)

explanation.surface: A crew of 504 sailors voyaging round a group of tropical islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The number is written as Roman numerals, D for five hundred and IV for four.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maldives are an archipelago of coral atolls in the Indian Ocean, a nation of many islands.

clue.text: Stocking filler for a little beast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the part of the leg that fills out a stocking

explanation.surface: A Christmas present bought for a small child or pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking filler' suggests a small Christmas gift, but it means the fleshy back of the lower leg inside a stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: The calf is the muscular rear of the lower leg, and also the young offspring of cattle.

clue.text: Cotton sari crumpled in drawer

indicators.note: crumpled cloth is creased out of shape, so these letters lose their original order

parts.note: both words rearranged together

explanation.surface: A creased cotton garment has been left in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like a furniture compartment but means one who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoonist is an artist who sketches comic pictures, so is literally someone who draws.

clue.text: Row for a change about Conservative leader

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other letter

parts.note: an alteration is a change

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter of the party name is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the party name

explanation.surface: A dispute in which the Tory chief is pushed out to make way for new blood.
explanation.walkthrough: Conservative leader is a single letter here, the standard abbreviation for the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Row, rhyming with cow, means a noisy quarrel, which is what an altercation is.

clue.text: A German saint and a German physicist

parts.note: ein is German for 'a'
St is the abbreviation for saint
again the German for 'a'

explanation.surface: A list pairing a German holy figure with a German scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A German' is not a person but the German word for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, born in Ulm, was the theoretical physicist behind the theory of relativity.

clue.text: In custody pending trial, one man died protecting ringleader

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the outer letters wrap round the inner one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
d is the abbreviation for died
the leader, or first letter, of ring

explanation.surface: A prisoner awaiting trial; one man died while shielding the gang boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringleader' looks like a gang boss but is just the first letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant on remand is held in detention while waiting for the case to be heard.

clue.text: Members of a priestly class drop in to see a composer

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so the two letters that follow are removed

parts.note: Brahmins are the Hindu priestly caste
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Priests pop by to visit a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop in' reads as visiting, but it is an instruction to take the letters IN out of the caste name.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer of symphonies, concertos and the famous lullaby.

clue.text: Neil is drunk and stays in bed

definitions.note: the clue's verb phrase stands for the plural noun

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters of that name are jumbled

parts.note: a man's name, rearranged with the next word
taken as written and rearranged

explanation.surface: Neil gets plastered and doesn't get up in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' does double duty: it is part of the fodder and of the anagram signal 'is drunk'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a lazy morning spent sleeping late, so stays in bed are lie-ins when read as nouns.

clue.text: Source of article in part of France

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the short word sits within the region name

parts.note: Provence is a region of southern France
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Tracing where some item came from to a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Provenance is the place of origin or history of ownership of something, hence its source.

clue.text: Queen surrounded by brass snakes

indicators.note: something surrounded by another is enclosed in it, so the monarch's letters go inside

parts.note: top brass are very important persons
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch hemmed in by brass serpent ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like the metal but means senior officers or bigwigs, as in 'top brass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vipers are venomous snakes, including the adder, Britain's only poisonous species.

clue.text: Pledge oneself to come into battle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: commit or promise, as in an engagement to marry
second meaning: join combat with an enemy

explanation.surface: A soldier vowing to join the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage means both to bind oneself by promise and to enter combat with opposing forces.

clue.text: Almost regretting destruction

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is cut

parts.note: ruing means regretting

explanation.surface: Nearly sorry about the wreckage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is the state of being destroyed or wrecked, a straightforward synonym of devastation.

clue.text: Tea and pieces of pitta bread

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

indicators.note: broken into pieces, the word that follows is reassembled in another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An afternoon snack of tea with torn-up flatbread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitta bread' looks like one item, but the bread is the definition and only 'pitta' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapatti is an unleavened Indian flatbread cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: Vaulting ambition involves a piece of gamesmanship

indicators.note: to involve is to contain within, so the answer is held inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the run straddling the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Overreaching ambition, as in Macbeth, depends on cunning tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaulting ambition' is Macbeth's phrase; the answer spans its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move, originally in chess, made to gain an advantage, a calculated ploy.

clue.text: Undiluted sound in passage

indicators.note: sound means as heard, so the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a straight drink is undiluted

explanation.surface: A neat spirit's noise inside a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' could itself be a sea channel, but here it signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of water connecting two seas, a passage for ships.

clue.text: First-class men required as spies

parts.note: A, as in A1, means first-class
gents is short for gentlemen

explanation.surface: Top-quality chaps are wanted to work in espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: A for first-class comes from A1, the top rating.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret agents are operatives working for intelligence services, that is, spies.
